Ballyroan 
The development of Ballyroan Playground, Multi-Use Games Area and Amenity 
with Car Park at the site of the Old Boys’ National School (TVRS) has been 
completed. The Playground, MUGA, Amenity and Car Park were officially opened 
by Laois County Council’s Regeneration Section in conjunction with Sports and 
Leisure Section and the Ballyroan Community Development CLG on 23rd June 
2026 to an enthusiastic audience of local children and residents. The opening was 
compered by Town Regeneration Officer, Denise Rainey. The audience was 
addressed by Cathaoirleach Cllr Barry Walsh, native of Ballyroan, Regeneration 
& Economic Development’s Director of Services, Angela McEvoy and Ballyroan 
Community Development CLG’s Chair, Mary Whelan. Representatives from 4th 
Class, Scoil Eoin Phóil II Naofa who won a competition to name the facility Croí an 
Bhaile (Heart of the Village) spoke about what the amenity means to them.  
They along with winners of the colouring competition received prizes at the 
event.  The facility was blessed by Father Petru (Peter) Medves and Reverend 
Canon, Patrick Harvey.  The children tested out all the equipment to much 
excitement on the day. The children were treated to ice creams from the local 
shop. Refreshments were served on the site thanks to Laois County Council and 
Ballyroan Community Development CLG in the community hall. All involved in the 
project were commended for their efforts and for the organisation of a fully 
attended launch event.

Vacancy / Regeneration Funding Schemes  
A Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant is available for up to a maximum of €50,000, including 
VAT, for refurbishment of vacant properties for use as a principle private residence or to be made 
available for rent, including the conversion of a property which has not been used as residential 
heretofore.   A top-up grant of up to €20,000 is also available for properties which are derelict.  
An on-line application system for the Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant was introduced in 
Laois County Council on 11th June, 2026.   The new system will make it easier for applicants to 
apply, with all documentation and supporting resources stored within their own personal account.  
The new system will enhance the Council’s efficiency of application processing.  All new 
applications from 11th June, 2026 must be submitted on-line only.

The Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant has been expanded, with effect from 31st March 2026, 
to support bringing more vacant and derelict properties into use as homes. This includes the 
provision of top-up amounts to existing grant levels where vacant former commercial/public use 
buildings are being converted in their entirety into two or more residential units. 
 
From 31st March 2026, the following grants are also available: 
 
Vacant Above the Shop Grant 
A grant of up to €135,000 is available for the conversion or refurbishment of vacant above shop 
space into residential units for occupation as a principal private residence and/or for residential 
units), subject to appropriate planning permission being in place.  Where one residential unit is

two residential units are being created up to €115,000 is available and where three or more units 
are created up to €135,000 is available. 
 
The Grant applies to vacant ‘above the shop’ space in buildings in cities, towns and villages, where 
the building was built prior to 2008 and the space/existing residential unit(s) have been vacant for 
two years or more prior to application. The ground floor commercial space may be vacant or in use 
at time of application but must be remaining in commercial use.  
 
Expert Advice Grant 
An Expert Advice Grant is available for Vacant Above the Shop Conversions and Conversion of 
former commercial / public use buildings to residential units.  The Expert Advice Grant provides 
funding of up to €5,000 towards having an appropriately qualified professional provide expert 
advice to the owner of;  
  
• 
A building with a commercial element and vacant above the shop space who may avail of 
the Vacant Above the Shop Grant to convert / refurbish the vacant space into residential 
unit/s, with the commercial element remaining. 
• 
A former vacant commercial / public use building who may avail of the Vacant Property 
Refurbishment Grant Conversion of former Commercial Building / public use building to 
convert the entire building into more than one residential unit. 
 
Only one Expert Advice grant can be applied for per building.  Applications can only be made by 
named individuals who own the building for which the advice grant is being applied, or who are 
actively engaged in purchasing the building. Where there is more than one owner of the building, 
all owners must be included on the application form. The Expert Advice Grant is not currently 
available to registered companies, developers, undertakings etc.

Strong Engagement Across Training, Mentoring and Business 
Supports in LEO Laois January - June 2026 
 
 
 
LEO Laois delivered strong supports to local businesses in the first half of 2026, with 390 
participants across 31 training courses and 93 businesses supported through one-to-one 
mentoring. Demand for targeted programmes remained high, with approvals including 15 Green 
for Business, 16 Digital for Business, 6 Lean for Business, 6 Grow Digital Vouchers, and 12 Energy 
Efficiency Grants, alongside 11 businesses assisted in accessing Microfinance Ireland funding. 
These supports have helped businesses improve skills, adopt digital tools, enhance efficiency, 
reduce costs, and strengthen their capacity to grow, creating a positive impact on the local 
economy.

National Enterprise Awards 
 
 
 
Honor Deevy , Aymar Gourdet, Cllr Bary Walsh Cathaoirleach, Lisa Molloy Head of Enterprise and Angela McEvoy Director of Services at the 
National Enterprise Awards 
 
Le Skinny Chef Ltd. represented LEO Laois at the National Enterprise Awards on 18th June in the 
Mansion House, Dublin. The awards showcase the strength and diversity of Ireland’s micro-
enterprise sector and recognise businesses supported by the Local Enterprise Offices. 
While not securing an award on this occasion, Le Skinny Chef’s selection to represent Laois is a 
strong endorsement of the company’s growth, innovation and ambition. Founded in 2016 by 
award-winning chef Aymar Gourdet, the business continues to demonstrate excellence in product 
development and market expansion, supported by LEO Laois through a range of financial and 
advisory supports.  Participation at national level provides valuable exposure and reinforces the 
company’s position as a leading enterprise within the region. 
 
 
Laois Women in Business Event 
 
LEO Laois hosted a Women in Business networking lunch on 26th May in Batoni’s Restaurant, Emo, 
as part of its 2026 programme supporting female entrepreneurship across the county. The event 
was fully subscribed, with 80 attendees, and provided an excellent opportunity for local business 
owners to connect, share experiences and build networks. 
 
The event featured engaging and informative contributions from Alison O’Kelly, AOK 
Communications, who delivered insights on developing a personal brand online, and guest speaker 
Katelyn Cummins, Rose of Tralee. The event was expertly facilitated by MC Sally-Ann Barrett of 
Midlands 103.

Business Advice Clinics 
 
LEO Laois is delivering a series of Lunch & Learn sessions and Business Clinics across the county 
as part of its proactive outreach programme to increase awareness and accessibility of supports 
for local businesses. These events provide valuable opportunities for entrepreneurs and business 
owners to engage directly with the LEO team, receive tailored advice, and learn more about the 
supports available to start and grow their business. 
 
The next event, a Lunch & Learn session, will take place on Thursday, 25th June in Stradbally 
Library, offering an informal setting for businesses to connect, gain insights, and ask questions. 
Further Lunch & Learns and Business Clinics are planned in locations across the county over the 
coming months, ensuring broad geographic reach and engagement with both new and existing 
clients. This outreach initiative plays a key role in strengthening connections with the local business 
community and driving increased uptake of LEO supports. 
 
Showcase 
Applications were received for Showcase 2027, and it has been confirmed that four Laois LEO-
supported businesses will exhibit at the event in January 2027. The participating companies are 
Alison McEvoy (Artist), Carlow Resin Crafts, Catherine Hearns (MyComfort), and Santiago 
Lonigro (Santilonigro Art). 
 
Participation in Showcase provides a significant commercial opportunity for these businesses, 
offering exposure to national and international buyers, retailers, and distributors. Exhibiting at this 
flagship event enables companies to develop new sales channels, increase brand visibility, and 
secure export opportunities, while also gaining valuable market insights and industry connections. 
This engagement highlights the continued support of LEO Laois in helping local businesses scale, 
access new markets, and strengthen their competitiveness both nationally and internationally. 
 
 
National Ploughing Championships Local Village 2026 
Le Skinny Chef Ltd. has been selected to represent LEO Laois in the Local Enterprise Village at the 
National Ploughing Championships 2026. The Local Enterprise Village, an initiative of the Local 
Enterprise Offices, will showcase 30 small businesses from across the country and will be located 
at the centre of the event in Screggan, Co. Offaly from 15th to 17th September.

Economic Development Update – Key Activities and Initiatives 
 
Streetscape Schemes 
The Mountmellick and Ballinakill Streetscape Schemes closed for applications on 1 June 2026. The 
schemes are designed to support the upgrade and enhancement of buildings within designated 
areas of both towns through grant assistance for external painting works. 
 
Funding is provided at a rate of 75% of total eligible painting costs, up to a maximum of €1,000 per 
property.

Shop Front Improvement & Accessibility Grant Scheme 
The Shop Front Improvement & Accessibility Grant Scheme aims to enhance the visual appeal and 
accessibility of independently owned retail premises along public streets. Eligible works include 
painting, signage replacement, and, where appropriate, full shopfront refurbishment. The scheme 
provides grant assistance of 50% of eligible costs, up to a maximum of €750 per property. 
 
To date, 10 applications have been received in 2026.  All works must be completed by 30 
September 2026, with grant claims due by 30 October 2026. 
 
Invest Laois / Marketing Campaign 
The Invest Laois website (www.investlaois.ie) launched at the end of May 2026, with an official 
launch event to follow. A targeted marketing campaign is currently in development in partnership 
with “We the People” to promote County Laois as a competitive and attractive location for both 
national and international investment. 
 
Laois continues to strengthen its positioning through its central location, excellent connectivity, 
strong transport infrastructure, and competitive operating environment. This is further supported 
by investment under the EU Just Transition Fund and the ongoing development of the strategic 
landbank at Junction 17, National Enterprise Park. 
Collectively, these initiatives reinforce the county’s long-term capacity to support sustainable 
enterprise growth. A key element of the campaign is the promotion of local business success 
stories, which highlight the practical advantages of locating in Laois and help position the county as 
a first-choice destination for investment.

Portlaoise Library are delighted to host Symbol of Hope – An Exhibition of Two Cultures 
from 8th–26th June 2026 as part of Refugee Week Ireland. This unique travelling 
exhibition celebrates the rich cultural heritage of Ukraine and Ireland through traditional 
costume, art, and craftsmanship. 
Visitors can explore eight mannequins dressed in authentic Ukrainian regional clothing 
alongside creative interpretations of historical Irish dress, highlighting the beauty, 
resilience, and traditions of both cultures. The exhibition also features intricate pysanky 
(decorated Ukrainian eggs), folk art, embroidery, pottery, and handcrafted decorative 
pieces that reflect generations of artistic expression and storytelling. 
Symbol of Hope has travelled to libraries, museums, and community spaces across Ireland 
since 2024, promoting cultural dialogue, unity, and mutual support between Ukrainian 
and Irish communities. Each display includes QR codes offering deeper insight into the 
garments, their regional origins, and the traditions behind them, allowing visitors to 
engage with the exhibition at their own pace.

Calling up Berba 
An exhibition of new work by resident artist Donna Wright at Laois Arthouse 
On Thurs 4th June Donna Wright shared artwork developed during her residency (May – 
June 2026) in an exhibition titled Calling Up Berba (4 – 13 June). This series of artworks 
explored the ecology and mythology of the River Barrow. Working on large streams of 
unstretched canvas Donna’s work expresses layered thinking, weaving mythological and 
biological readings of place.  For example, A breath away from gone, depicting a salmon 
wending among acorns and freshwater pearl mussels links the origin myth of the Barrow 
Goddess Berba with the current decline of the freshwater pearl mussel.  The exhibition 
opening was a very welcoming occasion with many attending, including artists travelling 
from neighbouring counties to view Calling up Berba and to meet Donna.  Donna also 
discussed what drew her to work in Ireland, her family heritage, about her overall 
approach, her immersion in Indigenous Australian forms of knowledge and their 
influences on her creative process.  
 
Dr. Donna Wright is an Australian born visual artist of Irish heritage and citizenship. Her 
professional research-led arts practice has spanned 35 years, with a national and 
international exhibiting profile. Donna has been a creative and cultural interface educator 
for 25 years pursuing a dedicated long-term objective of decolonising the western mind 
towards deep respect and gratitude for Indigenous ways of knowing and being. Through 
place-based international residencies and projects, Donna seeks out the stories 
intrinsically rooted in the deep and ancient relationships we form with the natural world. 
Donna’s longstanding familial and professional relationships with the Indigenous 
communities of what is now known as Australia has situated her political, ethical and moral 
values, and her ardent advocacy for Indigenous self-determination, particularly in 
continuing settler-colonial states.

Cruinniú na nÓg 2026 
This year’s Cruinniú na nÓg festival took place on Saturday, 6th June, and proved to be 
another wonderful success. The event continues to grow in both popularity and quality 
each year, attracting increasing levels of participation and engagement from children, 
young people, families, and communities across County Laois. 
A total of 26 individual events were delivered, ensuring a strong and balanced programme 
of activities spread throughout the county. The diverse range of events provided 
opportunities for all children and young people to explore creativity, culture, music, art, 
science, and community participation in a fun and inclusive environment. 
Many of the events were organised in partnership with key cultural partners, including 
Laois Libraries, Laois Arts Department, Dunamaise Arts Centre, and the Laois School of 
Music. The remaining activities were delivered by local youth groups, community 
organisations, and volunteers, highlighting the strong collaborative spirit that continues 
to underpin the festival. 
Among the events coordinated by emerging partners were family fun days at both the 
Portlaoise and Mountmellick Family Resource Centres, street art workshops delivered by 
Youth Work Laois, and a variety of dance and science activities hosted at Castletown 
Community Centre. Additional highlights included a songwriting workshop held in 
Abbeyleix Heritage House and the unveiling of a mural created by Traveller children at the 
Laois School of Music during the Laois Le Chéile Festival. These events showcased the 
creativity, talent, and enthusiasm of young people from across the county while 
encouraging participation in the arts and cultural life of their communities. 
It is estimated that approximately 500 children and young people attended Cruinniú na 
nÓg activities throughout County Laois this year. The strong attendance figures, together 
with the positive feedback received from participants, families, organisers, and community 
groups, demonstrate the continuing success and growing impact of the festival. Cruinniú 
na nÓg remains an important opportunity to celebrate youth creativity and provide 
accessible cultural experiences for children and young people across the county.

On 15th May the Heritage Council announced grants awarded under the 2026 
Community Heritage Grant Scheme. This scheme provides funding for a wide variety of 
community led heritage projects. The scheme receives an average of 400 applications 
annually with only 25% being awarded funding. 
 
The Erkina Blueway Association were among the successful groups awarded funding in 
2026 (€25,000 the maximum) towards their Waterwheel Restoration Project. This 
project aims to restore the waterwheel at Newtown Mill, Durrow. The project was 
initiated by the Erkina Blueway Association and is supported by Laois County Council 
Heritage Office in partnership with the group and the mill owner.  
 
The Laois Mill Survey states that Newtown Mill, Durrow “is of technical interest in retaining 
a working waterwheel (the only such wheel in the entire county), segment-wheel/ bull-nut power 
transmission, and an almost complete assemblage of primary machinery”.
